regulation.scope: Any system that processes personal data of EU/EEA data subjects, regardless of where the processor is established.

rules.title: Principles relating to processing of personal data
rules.description: Personal data must be processed lawfully, fairly, and transparently; collected for specified, explicit, and legitimate purposes (purpose limitation); limited to what is necessary (data minimisation); kept accurate; stored no longer than necessary (storage limitation); and processed with appropriate security (integrity and confidentiality). The controller is accountable for demonstrating compliance.
check_hints: Personal data fields collected beyond the declared purpose of the feature
No data retention / TTL policy enforced in database models or cache layers
Absence of a data minimisation review: forms or APIs requesting more fields than needed
PII logged to application logs (names, emails, IPs, device IDs) without pseudonymisation
No accountability trail: missing audit log for create/read/update/delete on personal data
Data shared with third parties without a documented legal basis or processor agreement
non_compliant_patterns: SELECT * FROM users — selecting all columns including PII when only ID is needed
console.log(user) — logging full user objects containing PII
INSERT INTO analytics (user_email, ...) — storing PII in analytics tables without purpose check
No cron job or scheduled task to purge expired personal data records
rules.remediation_guidance: Implement a Data Processing Register (ROPA). Add column-level annotations for PII fields. Enforce retention policies via scheduled jobs. Replace full-object logging with structured logging that omits or pseudonymises PII fields.

rules.title: Lawfulness of processing — legal basis
rules.description: Processing of personal data is lawful only if at least one of six legal bases applies: (a) consent of the data subject; (b) performance of a contract; (c) compliance with a legal obligation; (d) protection of vital interests; (e) public task; or (f) legitimate interests of the controller, provided they are not overridden by the interests of the data subject.
legal_bases: Art.6(1)(a) — Consent (must be freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous)
Art.6(1)(f) — Legitimate interests (requires Legitimate Interests Assessment)
check_hints: Processing of personal data with no consent gate, contract linkage, or documented legal basis
Consent collected but not recorded with timestamp, version of privacy notice, and scope
Processing commences before consent is confirmed (race condition in async consent flows)
Consent bundled together with terms of service — not freely given or specific
Legitimate interest used as a catch-all without a documented LIA on file
Email marketing sent without explicit opt-in consent
Data subject's personal data processed after consent is withdrawn
non_compliant_patterns: sendMarketingEmail(user.email) called without checking user.marketing_consent === true
User profile created and data processed before consent confirmation callback resolves
Single checkbox: 'I agree to Terms of Service and Privacy Policy and marketing'
No consent record table or consent_log in the database schema
rules.remediation_guidance: Implement a ConsentService that gates all personal-data processing. Store consent records with data_subject_id, timestamp, privacy_notice_version, scope[], and ip_address. Handle consent withdrawal by immediately halting processing and propagating deletion/suppression signals.

rules.title: Conditions for consent
rules.description: Where processing is based on consent, the controller must be able to demonstrate that the data subject has consented. Requests for consent must be presented in an intelligible and easily accessible form, using clear and plain language. The data subject has the right to withdraw consent at any time as easily as to give it.
check_hints: No mechanism to record timestamp, identity, and affirmative action of consent
Consent cannot be withdrawn as easily as given (missing withdrawal handler)
Pre-ticked checkboxes or bundled consent terms with contract performance
non_compliant_patterns: checkBox.setChecked(true) by default
No withdrawConsent() or revokeConsent() method provided in user settings
Consent required as a condition of service where not strictly necessary
rules.remediation_guidance: Implement granular, unbundled opt-in consent mechanisms with easily accessible withdrawal options and verifiable consent logs.

rules.title: Child consent conditions in relation to information society services
rules.description: Where the data subject is a child under 16 years (or Member State threshold not below 13), processing based on consent is lawful only if consent is given or authorized by the holder of parental responsibility. Controllers must make reasonable efforts to verify parental consent.
check_hints: App accessible to children without age-gating or birth date verification
No parental consent verification mechanism for underage users
non_compliant_patterns: Collecting child profile data without age verification check
No parental email confirmation or authorization flow before activating child account
rules.remediation_guidance: Implement age-verification gating and verifiable parental consent authorization flows for minors.

rules.title: Processing of special categories of personal data
rules.description: Processing of personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, trade union membership, genetic data, biometric data for uniquely identifying a person, health data, or sexual orientation is prohibited unless an Article 9(2) exception applies.
check_hints: Collecting biometric, health, genetic, religious, or political data without explicit Art. 9(2) legal ground
Special category data stored in general analytics or logs without enhanced protection
non_compliant_patterns: Storing fingerprint or facial geometry templates without biometric consent exception
Logging medical diagnosis, prescription, or health telemetry in application logs
rules.remediation_guidance: Cease processing special category personal data unless covered by an explicit Article 9(2) exemption and secured by dedicated encryption.

rules.title: Transparent information and modalities for exercising data subject rights
rules.description: The controller must provide information and communications relating to data processing and data subject rights in a concise, transparent, intelligible, and easily accessible form, using clear and plain language. Information must be provided free of charge and within one month of receipt.
check_hints: Opaque or convoluted privacy terms hidden behind multiple redirects
No workflow tracking to ensure data subject requests are answered within 30 days
non_compliant_patterns: Charging fees for standard privacy requests
No request tracking queue or SLA enforcement for privacy inquiries
rules.remediation_guidance: Provide concise, layered privacy notices and establish automated request tracking ensuring responses within 30 days.

rules.title: Information to be provided where personal data are collected from the data subject
rules.description: When collecting personal data directly from the data subject, the controller must provide at collection time: identity/contact details of controller and DPO, purposes and legal basis, recipients, retention period, and the existence of data subject rights.
check_hints: Collecting registration fields, GPS location, or device ID without a privacy notice at the point of capture
Third-party analytics SDKs initialized without disclosing recipients to the user
non_compliant_patterns: Registration form submitting PII without displaying privacy policy notice or link
Tracking SDK initialized before privacy notice is displayed
rules.remediation_guidance: Display in-context privacy notices with links to the full policy at every data capture point.

rules.title: Information to be provided where personal data have not been obtained from the data subject
rules.description: Where data are not obtained from the data subject, the controller must inform the subject of the source, categories of personal data, purposes, and recipients within a reasonable period (at most one month), or at the latest upon first communication with the subject.
check_hints: Ingesting contact lists, address books, or external broker data without notifying affected subjects
Silent enrichment of user profiles from third-party social or tracking sources
non_compliant_patterns: syncContacts() uploading non-user phone numbers without notification mechanism
Third-party marketing data merged into profiles without notifying the data subject
rules.remediation_guidance: Send privacy notices to indirectly acquired contacts within 30 days, or avoid storing third-party PII without a communication channel.

rules.title: Right of access by the data subject
rules.description: The data subject has the right to obtain confirmation as to whether their personal data are being processed and access to a copy of their personal data, along with details of processing purposes, categories, recipients, and retention periods.
check_hints: No endpoint or interface allowing users to view or export a full copy of their personal data
Data access reports omit secondary data, analytics profiles, or behavioral tracking logs
non_compliant_patterns: GET /profile returns basic fields while hidden profiling records are withheld
Absence of a self-service data download endpoint
rules.remediation_guidance: Implement a comprehensive Data Subject Access Request (DSAR) export service providing complete personal data records.

rules.title: Right to rectification
rules.description: The data subject has the right to obtain from the controller without undue delay the rectification of inaccurate personal data concerning them, and the completion of incomplete personal data.
check_hints: User profile attributes are immutable and cannot be updated by the user or support
Downstream replicas or search caches do not sync when personal data is corrected
non_compliant_patterns: API rejects updates to core profile fields such as name, email, or address
No event emission to propagate profile corrections to downstream systems
rules.remediation_guidance: Provide user-facing profile correction endpoints and propagate updates to all data stores and third-party processors.

rules.title: Right to erasure ('right to be forgotten')
rules.description: Data subjects have the right to obtain erasure of their personal data without undue delay when: the data is no longer necessary for the purpose collected; consent is withdrawn and no other legal basis applies; the subject objects and there is no overriding legitimate interest; the data was unlawfully processed; or erasure is required by law. The controller must also inform any processors or third parties to whom data was disclosed.
check_hints: No erasure endpoint or handler (e.g. DELETE /users/{id} or AccountDeletionService)
Erasure handler deletes from primary table but leaves PII in: audit logs, analytics tables, search indexes, data warehouse, backups, CDN caches, or third-party integrations
Erasure is soft-delete only (deleted_at flag) with PII still readable in the database
No propagation to downstream processors — third-party services not notified on erasure
Erasure request queued but no SLA enforced (GDPR requires 'without undue delay', max 30 days)
Pseudonymisation used for erasure but a re-identification key is retained
No mechanism to handle erasure of data in event-sourced systems or immutable logs
non_compliant_patterns: UPDATE users SET deleted_at = NOW() WHERE id = ? — soft delete, PII still in DB
DELETE FROM users WHERE id = ? — primary table only, backup/analytics not cleaned
No call to stripe.customers.del(), sendgrid suppression list, or similar on account deletion
Erasure handler returns 200 OK without verifying all data stores were cleared
rules.remediation_guidance: Implement a choreography-based erasure saga that publishes a UserErasureRequested event consumed by every service storing personal data. Track erasure task completion per data store. Store only a pseudonymous tombstone record. Schedule verification that PII is absent from all downstream sinks within 30 days.

rules.title: Right to restriction of processing
rules.description: The data subject has the right to obtain restriction of processing where accuracy is contested, processing is unlawful, data are needed for legal claims, or pending objection verification. Restricted data may only be stored, not further processed.
check_hints: No mechanism or database flag to pause processing on disputed personal data records
Restricted accounts continue to be processed in background analytics or batch jobs
non_compliant_patterns: Disputed account records processed normally by marketing or automated billing jobs
Absence of processing_restricted boolean column on user models
rules.remediation_guidance: Introduce a processing_restricted flag in data models and gate all automated workflows to skip restricted records.

rules.title: Right to data portability
rules.description: The data subject has the right to receive personal data concerning them in a structured, commonly used, and machine-readable format (e.g. JSON, CSV), and have it transmitted directly to another controller where technically feasible.
check_hints: Data export only offered in non-machine-readable formats such as static PDF or screenshots
Absence of automated export endpoint for user-provided data
non_compliant_patterns: exportUserData() outputs non-standard proprietary binary or image format
No structured data download handler for user transaction and activity history
rules.remediation_guidance: Provide an asynchronous download endpoint that packages user-generated data into standard JSON or CSV files.

rules.title: Right to object
rules.description: The data subject has the right to object at any time to processing based on legitimate interests or public tasks, and an absolute right to object to processing for direct marketing, including profiling.
check_hints: No opt-out toggle for direct marketing, targeted ads, or behavioral analytics
Marketing notifications sent after user has opted out or unsubscribed
non_compliant_patterns: Push notification dispatched without checking marketingOptOut status
No unsubscribe or objection webhook handler
rules.remediation_guidance: Add opt-out controls in account settings; immediately halt direct marketing and profiling upon objection.

rules.title: Automated individual decision-making, including profiling
rules.description: The data subject has the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, which produces legal effects or similarly significant impacts, unless authorized with suitable safeguards including human intervention.
check_hints: Automated credit scoring, loan rejection, or account banning without human review mechanism
No facility for data subjects to contest automated decisions or express their point of view
non_compliant_patterns: if (riskScore > threshold) terminateAccount() with no appeal workflow
AI model automated decisions executed with no human-in-the-loop review mechanism
rules.remediation_guidance: Incorporate human-in-the-loop review for high-impact decisions and provide an appeal interface for users.

rules.title: Data protection by design and by default
rules.description: Controllers must implement appropriate technical and organisational measures both at the time of designing the processing system and at the time of processing itself. By default, only personal data necessary for each specific purpose must be processed — this applies to the amount collected, the extent of processing, the storage period, and accessibility.
check_hints: No pseudonymisation or encryption applied to personal data fields in database models
API responses returning full PII objects when only a subset is required by the consumer
Default settings expose personal data: public profile pages, opt-out rather than opt-in marketing
Personal data accessible to all internal roles without role-based access control (RBAC)
No field-level access control: all columns returned regardless of caller's permission scope
PII present in URL query parameters (logged by proxies, bookmarks, referrer headers)
No privacy impact assessment (DPIA) artefact linked to high-risk processing features
Third-party SDKs/analytics scripts loaded without data-minimisation configuration
non_compliant_patterns: GET /api/users returns { id, name, email, phone, address, dob } to all authenticated callers
router.get('/search?query=john.doe@example.com') — PII in URL
User object passed directly to analytics SDK: analytics.identify(user)
No @Encrypted or @Pseudonymised annotation on PII columns in ORM models
Role check absent: if (user.isAdmin) — missing for read paths on personal data
rules.remediation_guidance: Apply the principle of least privilege at both the API (response shaping) and database (column-level grants) layers. Use pseudonymisation for analytics. Annotate PII fields in data models and enforce encryption at the ORM layer. Make privacy-preserving options the default (opt-in, not opt-out).

rules.title: Processor obligations and vendor compliance
rules.description: Controllers must only use processors providing sufficient guarantees to implement appropriate technical and organisational measures. Processing must be governed by a binding contract (Data Processing Agreement / DPA) specifying data scope and obligations.
check_hints: Sharing personal data with third-party SDKs, APIs, or SaaS vendors without DPA verification
Sub-processor onboarding without security assessment or contractual compliance terms
non_compliant_patterns: Transmitting raw user telemetry to third-party crash reporting service without processor agreement
Hardcoded third-party tracker sharing device identifiers without processor gate
rules.remediation_guidance: Verify and record Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) with all external services and SDKs processing personal data.

rules.title: Records of processing activities (ROPA)
rules.description: Each controller and processor must maintain a record of processing activities under its responsibility, documenting purposes, data subject categories, personal data categories, recipients, transfers, retention periods, and security measures.
check_hints: Personal data processing pipelines with no corresponding documentation in processing register
New database models or messaging topics containing PII undocumented in data catalog
non_compliant_patterns: Creating database table user_biometrics with no schema documentation or ROPA tag
Unregistered message queue emitting PII events without catalog entry
rules.remediation_guidance: Maintain an automated metadata catalog tagging every data model and pipeline with purpose, retention, and legal basis.

rules.title: Security of processing
rules.description: Controllers and processors must implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk, including: pseudonymisation and encryption of personal data; ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability, and resilience of systems; ability to restore data after an incident; and regular testing and evaluation of security measures.
security_measures: Art.32(1)(b) — Ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability, resilience
Art.32(1)(c) — Ability to restore availability after an incident
Art.32(1)(d) — Regular testing, assessing, and evaluating effectiveness
check_hints: Personal data stored in plaintext in the database (no encryption at rest)
Sensitive data transmitted over HTTP (not HTTPS/TLS 1.2+)
Encryption using deprecated algorithms: MD5, SHA-1, DES, 3DES, RC4, ECB mode
Hardcoded encryption keys or secrets in source code or config files
No key rotation mechanism for encryption keys protecting personal data
Missing TLS certificate validation (verify=False, InsecureSkipVerify=true)
Personal data in backups not encrypted with a separate key
No intrusion detection, anomaly alerting, or breach notification mechanism
Session tokens or JWTs containing PII without encryption (only signed, not encrypted)
No rate limiting or brute-force protection on authentication endpoints
non_compliant_patterns: password_hash = md5(password) — weak hashing algorithm
requests.get(url, verify=False) — TLS validation disabled
SECRET_KEY = 'hardcoded-secret-key-123' — hardcoded secret
AES cipher initialised in ECB mode — does not provide semantic security
jwt.decode(token, options={'verify_signature': False}) — signature not verified
db.connect('mysql://user:password@host/db') — credentials in connection string
No bcrypt/argon2/scrypt usage for password storage — plain SHA-256 used
rules.remediation_guidance: Use bcrypt, Argon2id, or scrypt for password hashing. Enforce TLS 1.2+ with valid certificates. Store secrets in a secrets manager (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager). Use AES-256-GCM for data at rest. Implement key rotation policies. Add anomaly detection alerts for unusual access patterns on personal data stores.

rules.title: Notification of personal data breach to supervisory authority
rules.description: In the case of a personal data breach, the controller must notify the competent supervisory authority without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours after becoming aware of it, unless unlikely to risk individuals rights and freedoms.
check_hints: No automated security incident logging or escalation pipeline to trigger 72-hour notice window
Data leak exception swallowed or logged at debug level without notifying security operations
non_compliant_patterns: catch (DataLeakException e) { /* silently ignore */ }
No security alerting for mass exfiltration or unauthorized database dumps
rules.remediation_guidance: Implement real-time alerting for data exfiltration anomalies and automated security incident triage workflows.

rules.title: Communication of personal data breach to the data subject
rules.description: When a personal data breach is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller must communicate the breach to the data subject without undue delay in clear and plain language.
check_hints: No customer breach notification template or automated broadcast communication channel
Failure to alert affected users when plaintext passwords or financial records are compromised
non_compliant_patterns: Security incident handled internally with no communication to compromised accounts
No mechanism to broadcast security advisories to impacted users
rules.remediation_guidance: Establish pre-approved customer breach notification templates and broadcast communication protocols for security incidents.

rules.title: General principle for transfers of personal data to third countries
rules.description: Any transfer of personal data to a third country or international organization may take place only if conditions in Chapter V are complied with, ensuring the level of protection guaranteed by GDPR is not undermined.
check_hints: Direct API calls transmitting EU personal data to foreign servers lacking adequacy decisions or SCCs
Cloud storage bucket or database located in non-adequate jurisdiction without transfer safeguards
non_compliant_patterns: uploadToS3("us-east-1", euUserData) without transfer safeguards or encryption
Calling overseas tracking endpoint with raw EU user IP and device data
rules.remediation_guidance: Enforce regional routing and ensure cross-border transfers to non-adequate third countries utilize Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs).

rules.title: Derogations for specific situations (cross-border transfers)
rules.description: In the absence of an adequacy decision or appropriate safeguards, transfer to a third country is permitted only on specific grounds, such as explicit informed consent of the data subject or necessary performance of a contract.
check_hints: Invoking cross-border transfer without explicit data subject consent or contract necessity justification
Using Article 49 derogations for repetitive, mass data transfers rather than occasional exceptions
non_compliant_patterns: Transferring entire user database overseas under one-time consent claim
Routine automated background sync to non-adequate servers without contract necessity check
rules.remediation_guidance: Obtain explicit informed consent specifying transfer risks, or restrict cross-border transfers to strictly occasional non-repetitive cases.
